utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask the English interpreter first of all if it is possible to do what we have considered, that is, invite you to read the highlighted portion of the document in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can do our best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "As for me as early as tomorrow I will ask the Supreme Command to, regardless of their extent, and I do not believe that they will be very extensive, to thoroughly familiarise themselves with these materials. I will also propose after this in the composition determined -- in a composition determined by the supreme commander, the president, to a lesser degree or extent to familiarise this composition with the positions." Now we need to turn the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We don't need to turn the page. Just leave it, please, where it is. Thank you, that does seem to resolve the matter, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think it does, Your Honour, although now I have themselves instead of itself, but that may be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we had themselves in an earlier version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I understand that to mean that the Supreme Command is something separate and distinct from the supreme commander himself, Mr. Milosevic, and that it was more than one individual and it is not the Supreme Command Staff, because the Supreme Command Staff -- this is a meeting of the Supreme Command Staff or of the collegium and they're discussing proposals to be put forward that General Ojdanic is going to ask the Supreme Command to review or acquaint itself with. So who were those persons on the Supreme Command, wasn't that Mr. Milutinovic and Mr. Djukanovic, and perhaps some others?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the name itself, the Supreme Defence Council, what this means is the country's defence, that's what it implies. I explained a while ago that the country 's --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, let me stop you. There's no reference to Supreme Defence Council here. I'm asking you about Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Supreme Command of the army comprises the president, based on the powers of the Supreme Defence Council, with his General Staff, or rather, the Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, that doesn't make any sense, does it, that's like the Supreme Command Staff is going to furnish materials to itself and then meet with the supreme commander. That doesn't make sense in the context of what we just read here, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you understood me. If I may just explain. There were evening briefings, and these were chaired by the Chief of Staff. The supreme commander did not attend these briefings. Based on conclusions from those briefings a report is drafted which is then submitted to the president the next morning, or rather, the Chief of Staff in the evening hours if the president is there familiarises him with it, and in addition to this submits to him in writing a document from that meeting underlining problems that he as the Chief of Staff cannot resolve. At the same time, this report is submitted to other members of the Supreme Defence Council. I talked about the federal prime minister, I talked about the president of the Republic of Serbia, and I think there are about 15 or 16 different addresses that this report is then submitted to. It is for this reason that he put it this way here, that he would ask the president or the supreme commander, whether in a smaller or a larger circle of people to familiarise themselves with these problems that the army was now facing in this continuing war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be a convenient time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I would like to be clear about the first sentence of the passage you read where you twice read: "I will ask the Supreme Command to thoroughly familiarise themselves with these materials." Does that mean the group of 15 or 16 people you've just referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's not the Supreme Command, but these are the most responsible people in the country who are responsible for the defence of the country. It is not only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, the sentence quite simply talks about the Supreme Command and asking them to thoroughly familiarise themselves with these materials; it doesn't refer to 15 or 16 other people, it doesn't refer to the Supreme Defence Council. So what is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I've already said the Supreme Command consists of the supreme commander with his staff; that is the Supreme Command. As for the rest, this being said, these are the most responsible people for the defence of the country who have their own degree of responsibility in accordance with the offices they hold. That is why he says here in a bigger or narrower composition depending on what the president decides. By your leave ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You do allow me to proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had enormous problems in terms of war technical equipment. We were under sanctions, so the equipment was obsolete, inefficient. The Chief of Staff could not resolve it on his own. Government intervention was required of one and the other. Also, higher levels were required. If he were commander, then the units of the civil defence and the units of civilian protection would be subordinated to the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, which is not regulated that way in the Law on Defence of the country. These units are subordinated to the minister of defence, and he is linked to the prime minister. It is from that point of view that he believed that it was necessary to have a broader meeting with the highest levels available to have these problems resolved, those problems that were tormenting him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Suitable time to interrupt, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we have to complete our sitting at this stage, Mr. Simic, and that means that you have to return tomorrow. Tomorrow we will be sitting from 11.00, so you have to be back ready to resume your evidence at 11.00. I particularly emphasise before you leave the importance of having no discussion of the evidence in this case with anyone between now and then. So please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you at 11.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 14th day of September, 2007, at 11.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.07 p.m.,
